title: AI Assessment and Consultation Report: Lumivaara Logistics
description: FAIR AI advisory assessment report following the structure and style of sample_report.docx.

sections.title: Assessment Details
sections.instructions: A two-column table of the key details of the assessment: company, industry, date, advisors and company participants.

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary
sections.instructions: One paragraph: the company, its AI maturity, the top-priority use case and its expected benefit, and the main recommendation.

sections.title: 2. Company Overview
sections.instructions: Founding and ownership, size, sites, services, customer segments, current pressures and strategic goals.

sections.title: 3. AI Maturity Level
sections.instructions: Current systems, current use of AI and automation, how the work is organised, and the company's motivation. End with the maturity rating and its justification.
required_items: AI maturity rating: Low, Moderate or High

sections.title: 4. Current Solution Development Stage
sections.instructions: The stage of the AI work (for example ideation or pilot), the use cases identified so far, how the relevant processes run today, and the objectives.
required_items: development stage of the AI solutions

sections.title: 5. Identified Use Cases and Prioritisation
sections.instructions: A table of the identified use cases with current process and pain point, expected benefit, feasibility and priority, followed by short prose on which use case comes first, which next and which is deferred, and why.

sections.title: 6. Validity of Concept and Authenticity of Problem Addressed
sections.instructions: Evidence that the problems are real and measurable, and which concept is closest to implementation.

sections.title: 7. Integration and Importance of AI in the Idea
sections.instructions: The role of AI in each use case, the technique, and how central it is compared with conventional methods or human work.

sections.title: 8. Identified Target Market and Customer Segments
sections.instructions: The customer base and segments, attitudes, and which segments the AI initiatives would affect first.

sections.title: 9. Data Requirement Assessment
sections.instructions: The data each use case needs, where it is held, its history and quality, and the gaps.

sections.title: 10. Data Collection Strategy
sections.instructions: Data strategy, owners, how data is recorded and governed, and what is needed to close the gaps.

sections.title: 11. Technical Expertise and Capability
sections.instructions: In-house skills, external partners, system landscape and readiness for change, and implications for delivery.

sections.title: 12. Risks, Compliance and Responsible AI
sections.instructions: Technical, organisational and compliance risks, how public AI tools are used and governed, data protection and ownership, public-sector or regulatory mitigations.

sections.title: 13. Budget and Funding
sections.instructions: Past investments in AI, the willingness to invest, the amount management is willing to commit, and funding options considered.
required_items: the amount management is willing to invest in AI

sections.title: 14. Expectations from FAIR Services
sections.instructions: What the company expects from the advisory service: scoping, advice, policy, training and funding support.

sections.title: 15. Recommendations
sections.instructions: A bulleted list of concrete recommendations made during the assessment: scope, data preparation, human-in-the-loop controls, what to postpone and why.

sections.title: 16. Next Steps and Action Items
sections.instructions: A table of agreed action items with the person responsible and the deadline, and the next meeting.

sections.title: Appendix: Sources
sections.instructions: A bulleted list of the source materials used, each with its type and date.

instructions:
- No source has automatic priority, by class or by date. Preserve unresolved contradictions concerning the same subject and applicable context; do not treat historical changes alone as contradictions.
- Cite each fact by its source file, and add the page, sheet or heading only when the source has one; recordings and photos have none, so cite them by file name alone.
- Use the (missing: ...) marker only for the items listed as missing and for a section's required items, never for other information the sources do not give. Where the evidence is missing, do not invent anything: write only the marker and add no inferred or loosely related text for that item or section. When a section's only content is the missing marker, write nothing else in that section, even if loosely related facts exist.
